data.name: Bijit
data.gender_notes: Bijit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bij' meaning seed and 'it' meaning 'conqueror'. This name signifies the one who conquers obstacles and is victorious in every aspect of life. The name Bijit carries the meaning “Victorious, Conqueror” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Bengali. Parents who choose Bijit usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious, conqueror and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a soul that is destined to overcome challenges and achieve success in all aspects of life.
data.etymology: Bijit belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victorious, Conqueror.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bijit total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Bijit' reflects the Hindu philosophical belief in overcoming challenges and adversity, much like the deity Lord Hanuman, who is known for his unwavering courage and unyielding spirit. It conveys the Indian cultural value of perseverance and the strength that comes from facing obstacles head-on.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name 'Bijit' signifies the conqueror of one's own inner demons and obstacles, on the path to self-realization and enlightenment. It encourages the pursuit of personal growth and the attainment of inner peace and happiness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Bijit symbolizes the triumph of knowledge and wisdom over ignorance and darkness. It is a reminder that just as a seed (bij) holds immense potential for growth, so too does each individual have the power to transform and illuminate their own lives through the pursuit of knowledge.

historical_references.reference: Bijit, also known as Vijayasena, was a king of the Sena Dynasty in Bengal, ruling from 1120 to 1150 CE.
Another Bijit, a Hindu king of the Kuninda Dynasty in ancient India, is mentioned in the Mahabharata as a contemporary of Bhishma Pitamaha.
